item.title: Ultrahomogeneous hypertournaments
item.description: arXiv:2611.07292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A $k$-hypertournament is a higher-arity generalisation of a tournament, consisting of a set together with an irreflexive $k$-ary relation such that the automorphism group of each substructure of size $k$ is the alternating group $\mathrm{A}_k$. We show that, for each $k \geq 3$, there are continuum-many non-isomorphic countable ultrahomogeneous $k$-hypertournaments, answering a question of Cherlin.
item.dc:creator: Rob Sullivan

item.title: A true $\Pi^0_1$ sentence independence of PA
item.description: arXiv:2611.07321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a true $\Pi^0_1$ sentence $\varphi$ which is independent of Peano Arithmetic. Moreover, if $\widehat{\phi}$ denotes its interpretation on $\omega$ as a sentence of set theory, then $\widehat{\phi}$ is a $\Pi^0_1$ sentence independent of ZFC.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Golshani

item.title: Free $T_n$-Heyting algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.07915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: ${T}_n$-Heyting algebras form a subvariety of Heyting algebras and are characterized by the property that a chain of prime filters in such an algebra has at most $n-1$ elements. We study some basic properties of these algebras and determine the structure and number of elements of the free ${T}_n$-Heyting algebra with a finite number $r$ of free generators, $FT_n(r)$.
item.dc:creator: Juan Manuel Cornejo, Andr\'es Gallardo, Paula Helt, Luiz Monteiro, Ignacio Viglizzo

item.title: Idiosynchromatic Poetry
item.description: arXiv:2611.08079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove equivalences of asymmetric partition relations involving natural numbers and products of weakly compact cardinals $\kappa$, infinite cardinals $\lambda<\kappa$ and natural numbers to certain classes of finitary problems in the theory of edge-coloured digraphs. We are able to determine three classes of Ramsey numbers exactly, typical examples in these classes are $r(\omega^2 2, 3)$, $r(\kappa\lambda 2, 3)$ and $r(\kappa\lambda 3, 3)$. We moreover provide general upper bounds for $r(\omega^2 m, 3)$ and $r(\kappa\lambda m, n)$.
item.dc:creator: Thilo Weinert

item.title: Solving polynomials in large pseudo-finite sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.08211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using techniques from model theory, we prove analogues of Rado's and S\'ark\"ozy's theorems on solutions to polynomial equations in dense sets of definable groups and fields equipped with well-behaved measures. As a special case, we adapt our results to pseudofinite structures, to deduce non-qualitative asymptotic results.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Vegnuti

item.title: An order-reversing embedding of Turing degrees into Arthur-Nimue-Merlin degrees (short version)
item.description: arXiv:2611.08319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Arthur-Nimue-Merlin degrees are a generalization of the Turing degrees introduced by Kihara as a tangible description of the partially ordered set of Lawvere-Tierney topologies on the effective topos (equivalently, subtoposes of the effective topos). They are defined in terms of a three-player game that introduces both angelic and demonic non-determinism into oracle queries. We construct an order embedding of the Turing degrees with their order reversed into the Arthur-Nimue-Merlin degrees, whose image we call the "co-Turing degrees"; we then study the order relationship of these co-Turing degrees with the (naturally embedded) Turing degrees within the Arthur-Nimue-Merlin degrees. This is a short version of arXiv:2603.19946, focused on the main results.
item.dc:creator: Jean Abou Samra, David A. Madore

item.title: Degree profiles of uniform polynomial consequences: Linear lower bounds for Nullstellensatz and Polynomial Calculus
item.description: arXiv:2611.07280v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper proves asymptotically optimal linear degree lower bounds for Nullstellensatz and Polynomial Calculus, yielding a four-way polynomial-versus-exponential proof-size classification for uniform polynomial consequences over fields of positive characteristic. The size bounds use full, explicit coefficient lists, including zeros. Apart from a fixed finite initial range, exactly one of four cases occurs: $\mathrm T_1$, bounded degree; $\mathrm T_2$, degree at least linear in the universe size $n$; $\mathrm T_3$, constant degree on some residue classes and at least linear degree on the others; or $\mathrm T_4$, infinitely many recurring finite degrees, with bounded-degree subsequences and finite $\Omega(n)$ peaks at arbitrarily large sizes. Thus the size patterns are polynomial bounds, exponential lower bounds, a periodic mixture, or polynomial subsequences with finite exponential peaks, respectively. Underivable targets have degree $\infty$, and both proof systems assign the same type. The result strengthens my 2008--2009 refutation classification and extends it to uniform consequences. The proof uses degree-preserving lifting with onset and period bounds linear in the degree. A common $p$-adic hardness spectrum describes the four types topologically. Distinguishing any two types is undecidable already for refutations. The linear degree bounds, four-way classification and pairwise undecidability results have been formalised and verified in Lean. The Lean formalisation, verification records and an accompanying tutorial are available in the supporting materials (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23965838).
item.dc:creator: S{\o}ren Riis

item.title: First-Order Model Checking on Monadically Dependent Graph Classes
item.description: arXiv:2611.08143v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Monadically dependent graph classes are those in which first-order logic cannot encode all graphs. They include all nowhere dense classes and all classes of bounded twin-width. We show that first-order model checking is fixed-parameter tractable on every monadically dependent graph class. Together with the known hardness result for hereditary classes that are not monadically dependent, this gives a complete characterization of the hereditary graph classes with fixed-parameter tractable first-order model checking. This resolves a central open problem in algorithmic model theory. Our proof combines ideas from structural graph theory (graph decompositions), finite model theory (locality of first-order logic), and model theory (counting types). In particular, we show that in monadically dependent classes, tuples of fixed length have only $|U|^{O(1)}$ types of fixed quantifier rank over any set of parameters $U$.
item.dc:creator: Jan Dreier, Nikolas M\"ahlmann, Szymon Toru\'nczyk

item.title: A simplified proof of the o-minimal Whitney Extension Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2603.14924v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a proof of the o-minimal version of the Whitney Extension Theorem simplified as compared to the original ones. A new simplifying ingredient is a definable variant of Urysohn's lemma for class $\mathcal{C}^q$ (see Section 3).
item.dc:creator: Beata Kocel-Cynk, Wies{\l}aw Paw{\l}ucki, Anna Valette

item.title: Keisler Measures and Generically Stable Random Types
item.description: arXiv:2605.15870v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the notions of $rgs$ and $irgs$ for Keisler measures, motivated by the study of generically stable random types and their associated Morley sequences. We obtain characterizations of these notions in terms of averages of classical first-order formulas over suitable probabilistic partitions (Theorems 3.2 and 3.3). We compare these notions with $fim$, $fam$, and self-averaging, and show that for types the notions $fim$, $irgs$, and $rgs$ coincide. We prove that if a definable global Keisler measure$\mu$ is not dependent, then every Morley sequence in its canonical random extension $r_\mu$ is divergent (Theorem 4.7). Consequently, every $irgs$ measure is dependent (Corollary 4.8) and hence symmetric (Corollary 4.13). Furthermore, we show that for $irgs$ measures the model-theoretic instability events $\mathbf{O}^\varphi$, $\mathbf{I}^\varphi$, and $\mathbf{L}^\varphi$ have $\mathbb{P}_\mu$-measure zero (Theorem 5.4). In view of the equivalence of $fim$ and $irgs$ subsequently established in [6], this provides an alternative proof of the corresponding result for $fim$ measures in [9].
item.dc:creator: Karim Khanaki

item.title: Undecidability in Relevant Logic
item.description: arXiv:2605.29880v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove undecidability for every positive relevant logic extending the system axiomatized by hypothetical syllogism, prefixing, and suffixing and contained in the logic of the semilattice frame $(P_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathbb{N}), \cup, \varnothing)$. This settles the longstanding decision problem for the semilattice relevant logic S in the negative, contrary to prevailing expectations of decidability. It also provides a new proof of Urquhart's (1984) undecidability theorem for R, E, and T, now by reduction from the Wang tiling problem for arbitrarily large finite isosceles right triangular regions of the plane.
item.dc:creator: S{\o}ren Brinck Knudstorp

item.title: On various notions of universally Baire sets and reflection of non-Baire property in Cantor sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.36265v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Universally Baire sets are a standard tool in modern set theory, where they are closely connected with forcing and absoluteness. In this paper we study universal Baireness instead as purely a regularity notion for subsets of Polish spaces. Our aim is not to develop the set-theoretic theory, but to place the notion on a systematic descriptive-set-theoretic footing and to clarify the several nonequivalent definitions that occur in the literature. A subset of a Polish space is called \emph{universally Baire} if all its continuous preimages possess the property of Baire. However, it is important to specify what the domain of these continuous functions can be. In fact, a plethora of definitions are used by various authors in the literature, the class of possible domains is sometimes the class of Polish spaces, compact metrizable spaces, all topological spaces, compact topological spaces, etc. We clarify this situation by demonstrating that the above four options are pairwise nonequivalent under the Continuum Hypothesis, we determine all the implications between these four notions that are provable in $ZFC$, and also show that all the notions used in the literature are equivalent to one of these four. Furthermore, we use Miller forcing to show that actually the cases of Polish and compact metrizable spaces are consistently equivalent. We show that numerous definitions using Borel isomorphisms, changes of topologies and Boolean algebras are all equivalent to the case of Polish domains. We present an argument that the notion using Polish domains is the natural dual to the notion of universally measurable sets. Finally, as a byproduct, we prove that the following statement is independent of $ZFC$: if a subset of a Polish space has the property of Baire relative to every nowhere dense Cantor subspace, then the subset has the property of Baire in the whole space.
item.dc:creator: M\'arton Elekes, M\'at\'e P\'alfy

item.title: The Cone Fixing the Reals of $\mathrm{HOD}^{M_{2n}(x)}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.06032v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a cone of reals $x$, the reals of $\mathrm{HOD}^{L[x]}$ are precisely the reals in $Q_3$, or equivalently, the set of reals in $M_1$, the minimal proper class mouse with a Woodin cardinal. We show that if $z$ is any real coding $M_1|\delta^{+M_1}$, then $z$ is the base of such a cone (so $M_1^{\#}$ is such a base). We also establish a kind of optimality for this result, by identifying a real $x$ such that $M_1\subseteq L[x]$ but $\mathbb{R}\cap\mathrm{HOD}^{L[x]}\not\subseteq M_1$, although there is a base for the cone in a generic extension of $L[x]$. We prove an analogous result for the reals of $\mathrm{HOD}^{M_{n}(x)}$ for even $n$, as well as an analogous optimality result which holds for all $n$.
item.dc:creator: Farmer Schlutzenberg, Connor Watson
